source.name: Form fields inside a disabled fieldset must not be treated as tabbable, so a focus-trapped dialog focuses its first usable field
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/tabbable/issues/413) at cc8b7b2bc4319b672d0e6053b34c732168dd035c. Blind to the maintainers' fix 1d5fcb51d9eb21994c82a2f03010bc0d017cfff2; routing auto.

journey.title: Opening the address dialog puts focus on the first usable field
journey.goal: A keyboard user can open the dialog, type an address and save it

functionalJourney.title: Save the address dialog with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, saves and closes

success.value: Delivery address saved without a street.

functional.value: Delivery address saved without a street.

guards.title: Escape closes the address dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's delayInitialFocus option defers setting initial focus via setTimeout, so focus remains on the opening button when the test checks immediately after the dialog opens.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable the delayInitialFocus option when creating the focus trap so that initial focus is applied synchronously during activation.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive focus on the street input field immediately when the address dialog opens, enabling them to type without an extra Tab press.
functional_risks: Potential minor timing difference for assistive technologies that expect a delayed focus, but unlikely to cause adverse effects.
verification_requirements: After opening the dialog, focus must be on #street.
Typing an address and pressing Save must update the status correctly.
Pressing Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
The dialog must still be dismissible via Cancel button.

reasons: Keyboard candidate: failed · Step 2 · #street: expected "#street", observed "#open"

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's delayInitialFocus: true default defers initial focus via setTimeout, so focus remains on the opening button when the test checks immediately after dialog activation. Additionally, the automatic initial focus detection depends on tabbable node discovery which may not align with the test's synchronous expectation.
plan.repair_strategy: Explicitly configure initialFocus to target the street input (#street) and set delayInitialFocus: false to ensure synchronous focus during trap activation.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, initialFocus: '#street', delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive focus on the street input field immediately when the address dialog opens, enabling them to type without an extra Tab press.
functional_risks: Minimal risk: explicit focus target ensures correct behavior even if tabbable node detection timing varies.
verification_requirements: After opening the dialog, focus must be on #street.
Typing an address and pressing Save must update the status correctly.
Pressing Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
The dialog must still be dismissible via Cancel button.
